top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a mature, clean and reproducible discovery: magic-wavelength trapping lets many atoms be interrogated free of Doppler, recoil and light-shift errors, and independent laboratories have shown 10^-18 accuracy and stability. The allocation to Katori (the invention) and Ye (the realisation and development to the 10^-18 regime) is the natural one, and the citation is scoped to the lattice clock rather than to all of optical metrology, whose earlier core was already recognised. No award is the weaker option when a robust, fully demonstrated achievement is ready.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no direct link to the lattice-clock laureates, only general WACQT and Chalmers ties to precision quantum physics
